nameStory: The Common Eyelash gets its charming name from the distinctive dark hairs that ring the edge of its tiny red cup, looking exactly like eyelashes framing a bright eye. These 'eyelashes' are so prominent that the fungus has earned several whimsical nicknames including 'Molly eye-winker' and 'eyelash pixie cup.' It's one of those perfect nature names where you instantly understand exactly what the namers were seeing!
description: The Common Eyelash is a tiny, bright red cup-shaped fungus that looks like nature's smallest tea cup decorated with dark eyelashes. These saprophytic fungi (meaning they feed on dead organic matter) form small scarlet cups that are typically less than half an inch across. The cups have a smooth, bright red interior and are ringed with long, dark hairs that stick out like eyelashes. You'll usually find them growing in small groups on rotting wood, creating little clusters of what look like miniature red eyes peering up at you.

idTips.label: Eyelash hairs
idTips.description: Long, dark brown to black hairs stick straight out from the cup's rim like thick eyelashes - easily visible with a magnifying glass and the most reliable identifying feature

idTips.label: Cup shape
idTips.description: Bright scarlet-red cups that are shallow and saucer-like, with smooth interiors that feel slightly waxy to the touch

idTips.label: Size
idTips.description: Tiny fungi, typically less than half an inch across - small enough that you could fit several on a quarter

idTips.label: Growing pattern
idTips.description: Usually appears in small clusters or groups rather than alone, sometimes forming dense patches on suitable wood

idTips.label: Substrate preference
idTips.description: Almost always found on rotting wood that feels soft and damp, occasionally on other decaying organic matter in very moist conditions

idTips.label: Color consistency
idTips.description: Maintains its bright red color even when dry, though it may fade slightly - never yellow, orange, or brown

habitat: Look for Common Eyelash on rotting logs, stumps, and fallen branches in moist, shaded areas throughout New England's forests. They thrive in deciduous and mixed woodlands where dead wood stays consistently damp, often near streams, in ravines, or under dense canopy cover. You'll find them from sea level to mid-elevations, particularly in areas with rich, humid microenvironments where decomposition is active.

seasonality.spring: Fruiting bodies begin appearing as temperatures warm and moisture increases, often found on logs that have stayed wet through snowmelt and spring rains.
seasonality.summer: Peak season for Common Eyelash, with fresh bright red cups appearing regularly in humid conditions. Look for them after rainy periods when dead wood is thoroughly soaked.
seasonality.fall: Continue fruiting through autumn, especially during wet weather. The bright red cups provide striking color contrast against fallen leaves and darkening wood.
seasonality.winter: Rarely active in freezing temperatures, though old dried cups may persist on logs. Fresh fruiting resumes during winter thaws in milder areas.

funFact: Despite being found on every continent on Earth, Common Eyelash is so small that you could fit over 100 of them in the palm of your hand - yet those tiny 'eyelashes' are actually specialized cells that help launch spores into the air with remarkable precision!
confusionNotes: The distinctive eyelash hairs make this nearly impossible to confuse with other fungi once you know what to look for. Other small red cup fungi lack the prominent dark hairs, while other Scutellinia species require microscopic examination to distinguish. Memory trick: If it's a tiny red cup with obvious dark hairs on the rim, you've found your Common Eyelash!
contextualKnowledge: The scientific name Scutellinia comes from the Latin word for 'small shield,' referring to the cup's shape, while 'scutellata' means 'bearing small shields.' This species is considered the 'type species' for its entire genus, meaning it's the official standard that all other Scutellinia species are compared against.
compareHints: Common Eyelash is the most widespread of the eyelash cups and typically has the most prominent, darkest hairs. Yellow Eyelash Cup has yellowish coloring instead of bright red, while other Scutellinia species often have shorter, less noticeable hairs or require microscopic features for identification. The bright red color combined with very obvious dark rim hairs makes Common Eyelash the easiest of its relatives to identify in the field.
